description: Agent GovCon: submit a vendor’s eligibility record with the solicitation’s set-aside and eligibility terms: the record with the vendor’s legal business name, its unique entity identifier, the entity registration status and the day it expires, each size or socioeconomic status the vendor represents (small business, 8(a), HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned, women-owned or economically disadvantaged women-owned), each NAICS code with whether the record shows the vendor small under it, each status certification with the day it expires, and each exclusion or debarment entry with its kind, agency, whether it is active and the day it ends; the solicitation with its number, set-aside, NAICS code and anticipated award date. The signed report gives the record and the solicitation, each represented status read against the record that supports it, the set-aside read against the statuses the record supports on the award date, the registration read against the award date, each exclusion entry, and the solicitation’s NAICS code read against the codes on the record, and counts them, and names a divergent record: a size or status the record does not support, a set-aside the record does not meet, an entity registration expired or expiring before the award date, an active exclusion or debarment entry, and a NAICS code unlike the solicitation’s; then an exclusion entry marked inactive or ended, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No represented status, no size under the solicitation’s code, no set-aside, no award date, no registration status or expiry, or no NAICS code on either record leaves those points unverified. A small business status reads against the size the record shows under the solicitation’s code, a socioeconomic status against a certification current on the award date, and codes by their digits. This reads the supplied record only and decides nothing about eligibility. Verdict govcon_eligibility_divergent, govcon_eligibility_partial, govcon_eligibility_unverified or govcon_eligibility_consistent. POST /api/govcon-eligibility-check. Reads the government contracting records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between contracting documents only: it never submits a bid or proposal, never registers or certifies a vendor in any government system, never contacts an agency and never decides eligibility or award, which stay with the contracting agency, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent GovCon reads government contracting records across the procurement lifecycle for consistency between the documents and the terms they answer to: a solicitation, a vendor’s eligibility record, a proposal or bid, a price proposal or pricing volume, an award notice, a contract modification, a deliverable or progress report and an invoice or payment voucher, each against its own sections and the notice it follows, the solicitation’s set-aside, eligibility, submission and pricing terms, the winning price and eligibility record, the base award and prior modifications, the deliverable schedule, or the payment terms and acceptance record it should agree with. The family reads procurement, the government buying goods and services under contract terms, and reads the records against each other. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-govcon-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-govcon/.
